newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel promises better burials for Black Hebrews.
newsitem.headline: Israel promises better burials for Black Hebrews.

text.p: Israel promised on Thursday to help the tiny Black Hebrews religious sect find a site more dignified to bury their dead than a plot wedged between a rubbish dump and a livestock crossing near a nuclear reactor.

"The burial situation is very disrespectful," Aviv Ben-Yehuda, spokesman for the African-American sect whose several thousand members claim to descend from the ancient Israelite tribe of Judah, told Israel radio.
"We have a piece of land on the edges of the city of Dimona next to the Dimona dump. On the other side are bedouin and everyone passes by with flocks, dogs, everything."
Ben-Yehuda said some 35 Black Hebrews, who are not recognised as Jews by Israeli religious authorities and do not carry Israeli citizenship, were buried at the site.
The sect, a wing of a U.S.-based community led by a former Chicago bus driver, has settled for decades in an abandoned immigrant centre in Dimona, a depressed desert town home to a nuclear reactor.
Israeli Deputy Minister of Religious Affairs Yigal Bibi told Ben-Yehuda on air he would personally commit himself to improving the burial situation.
"The Ministry of Religious Affairs is concerned that every man of every religion be buried properly whether he be Jew, Christian or Moslem," Bibi told the radio.
Bibi, an Orthodox Jew, said the ministry and the Dimona municipality would provide funds to improve burial conditions for the Black Hebrews upon receipt of a formal request.

The Black Hebrews, who view themselves as the true children of Israel, refuse orthodox conversions to Judaism as a precondition for Israeli citizenship. They have had occasional run-ins with Israeli authorities who have sought to deport them.

An Interior Ministry spokesman told Reuters Israel was investigating attempts by Black Hebrew leaders in the United States to pass members through "apparent conversions" in order to gain Israeli citizenship and join the Dimona community.
The spokesman said the ministry was investigating citizenship requests by entire Black Hebrew families.
The sect adheres to a code of behaviour that requires members to be strict vegetarians and allows them up to seven wives.
